subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should OpenClaw core own failure-derived Skill Workshop repair plus usage-based skill retirement, or should maintainers first define a plugin/ClawHub extension boundary for those lifecycle decisions?
rationale: Current main only partially covers failed-turn user corrections; the remaining behavior adds persistent metrics, config, ranking/archive/delete policy, and possibly core skill discovery changes that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Split Core Design
options.body: Keep this open and split failure-derived repair from retirement so maintainers can design state, approval, and config semantics before implementation.

options.title: Plugin API First
options.body: Keep only the missing extension/API portion in core and route lifecycle policy to a plugin or ClawHub package once the API exists.

options.title: Close Not Planned
options.body: Close the lifecycle automation direction if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to infer skill edits or retirement from runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Split Core Design
recommendation.body: Keep this open and split failure-derived repair from retirement so maintainers can design state, approval, and config semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Skill Workshop capture/config/proposal implementation in blame is tied most directly to Shakker, so they are the best code-path owner from available history.
